title: Derived Hom continuity for bounded constructible etale complexes
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated Noetherian schemes with affine transition morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with limit $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Fix $i\in I$ and complexes $P_i,Q_i\in D^b((X_i)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] whose cohomology sheaves are constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Write $P_j,Q_j$ and $P,Q$ for their termwise inverse images at later stages and on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For every integer $n$, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{j\ge i}\operatorname{Hom}_{D((X_j)_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(P_j,Q_j[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(P,Q[n])$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups, compatible with composition, shifts, and passage to later stages. No local-freeness, projectivity, or finite-Tor assumption on the cohomology sheaves is imposed.

source.place: Agent finite Postnikov extension of lem-trf-constructible-etale-ext-continuity from sheaves to bounded complexes. Derived Categories, Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological, exact Hom sequences), together with the truncation triangles and exact filtered-colimit statements in the DAG. The etale-continuity inputs are those recorded in the sheaf Ext node; its cohomology-continuity source does not by itself assert this derived-Hom comparison.

proof.text: First treat a pair of constructible sheaves and their shifts. The cited Ext-continuity statement gives the canonical comparison as an isomorphism for every nonnegative degree. For a negative degree $n<0$, both Hom groups vanish: a sheaf $F$ concentrated in degree $0$ lies in $D^{\leq 0}$ of the standard t-structure, $G[n]$ lies in $D^{\geq -n}\subseteq D^{\geq 1}$ since its only cohomology sheaf sits in degree $-n\geq1$, and the orthogonality axiom gives $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\leq 0},D^{\geq 1})=0$; exact inverse image sends sheaves to sheaves, so the same holds at every stage and on $X$. Shifting the two sheaves identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(F_j[-a],G_j[-b+n])$ and its limit counterpart with the degree $n+a-b$ case. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism in every integer degree for all shifted constructible sheaves, and the Ext-continuity compatibility with later stages and composition is retained.

source.place: Tag 09YU with the shift reduction; negative-degree vanishing as in derived.tex Tag 06XS (lemma-negative-exts), here from the orthogonality axiom of the standard t-structure

proof.text: Fix a shifted constructible sheaf $Q$ and let $\mathcal C_Q$ be the bounded constructible objects $P$ for which the comparison is an isomorphism in every degree. Step 1 puts every shifted constructible sheaf in $\mathcal C_Q$. All triangles are formed at stage $i$ and pulled back: termwise inverse image is exact, hence a triangulated functor on derived categories that carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles and commutes with shifts, and it commutes with cohomology sheaves and canonical truncations, so the pulled-back triangles at every stage $j$ and on $X$ are distinguished and the pulled-back Postnikov tower of $P_i$ is the Postnikov tower of $P_j$ and of $P$. If $P\prime\to P\to P\doubleprime\to P\prime[1]$ is a distinguished triangle at stage $i$ with the outer objects in $\mathcal C_Q$, apply the Hom-out-of-a-triangle exact sequence to $Q_j[n]$ at every stage and to $Q[n]$ at the limit; the Hom-into statement supplies the vanishing of consecutive composites and the rotated exact segment. Filtered-colimit exactness gives an exact top row, and the canonical comparison maps form a commutative ladder because each is induced by a functor and the connecting morphisms of the pulled-back triangles are the pullbacks of the connecting morphism at stage $i$. The first, second, fourth and fifth vertical maps are isomorphisms by the outer hypotheses and shift closure, so the five lemma makes the middle map an isomorphism. Finally, if $\mathcal H^q(P_i)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, the truncation triangles $\tau_{\leq q-1}P_i\to\tau_{\leq q}P_i\to\mathcal H^q(P_i)[-q]\to(\tau_{\leq q-1}P_i)[1]$ for $q=a,\dots,b$, with $\tau_{\leq a-1}P_i\simeq0$ (in $\mathcal C_Q$ trivially) and $\tau_{\leq b}P_i\simeq P_i$, form a finite Postnikov tower whose graded pieces are the constructible cohomology sheaves shifted by their degrees. Induction on $q$ proves $P\in\mathcal C_Q$.

source.place: Tag 0149 (representable Hom exactness) and the canonical truncation triangles (Tag 08J5); filtered-colimit exactness is Tag 00DB and the ladder argument is Tag 05QB

proof.text: Now fix an arbitrary bounded constructible $P$ and let $\mathcal D_P$ be the objects $Q$ for which the comparison is an isomorphism in every degree. Step 2 puts every shifted constructible sheaf in $\mathcal D_P$. For a distinguished triangle $Q\prime\to Q\to Q\doubleprime\to Q\prime[1]$ at stage $i$, pulled back to every stage and to $X$ as in Step 2, with the outer objects in $\mathcal D_P$, use the Hom-into-a-triangle exact sequence at each stage and at the limit. The same filtered-colimit ladder and five-lemma argument, now with postcomposition maps, proves $Q\in\mathcal D_P$. The truncation triangles of $Q_i$ form a finite Postnikov tower, pulled back to every stage and to $X$, which has shifted constructible cohomology sheaves as its graded pieces, so a second induction proves the comparison for every $Q$. This establishes the displayed isomorphism for all bounded constructible $P,Q$ and all integers $n$.

source.place: Tag 0149 and finite Postnikov induction (canonical truncation triangles, Tag 08J5) on the second variable

proof.text: All comparison maps used above are induced by the exact inverse-image functors and their canonical derived composition isomorphisms. The associativity and identity equations for those isomorphisms identify the map of a composite with the composite of the two descended maps; the exact-functor Ext comparison gives the same assertion on the sheaf graded pieces. Naturality of the Hom long exact sequences and uniqueness in the five-lemma inductions then propagate this compatibility through every truncation triangle. The same argument with shift functors gives shift compatibility, and applying a later-stage inverse image to the construction gives passage-to-later-stages compatibility. Hence the isomorphism is canonical with all compatibilities claimed in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (derived inverse-image composition), together with derived.tex Tag 015F and functoriality in Tag 09YU

lean.statement: theorem bounded_constructible_derived_hom_continuity {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsNoetherian (D.obj i)] [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)] (c : Cone D) (_hc : IsLimit c) (i : I) {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [Finite A] (P Q : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (D.obj (op i)).smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) (hP : DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.bounded P ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, Scheme.IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Sheaf (D.obj (op i)).smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) q).obj P)) (hQ : DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.bounded Q ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, Scheme.IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Sheaf (D.obj (op i)).smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) q).obj Q)) : ∀ n : ℤ, BoundedConstructibleDerivedHomContinuityData D c P Q n
